about_blocks.text: About Executive Medical Solutions in Winnipeg

Executive Medical Solutions, often shortened to EMS, is a private outpatient addiction treatment program at 3408 Roblin Boulevard in Charleswood, in southwest Winnipeg. You live at home and keep working while you attend. The idea is that you practise new skills in the same places, relationships and routines that used to lead to drinking or drug use, instead of learning them away from home and coming back to everything at once.

about_blocks.text: Treatment is built around weekly one-to-one counselling and group therapy. Every client sees a counsellor each week, and the centre runs one to three groups a day that work through a set recovery topic each week. Counselling is trauma-informed and borrows from dialectical behaviour therapy (DBT) and cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT). Groups can be joined online, though the centre says coming in person works better.

about_blocks.text: What sets EMS apart from a counselling practice is the medical side. Psychiatrist Dr. Jeffrey Waldman, who has practised since 2003 and is certified by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Manitoba to prescribe Suboxone, assesses co-occurring mental illness, usually in the first week. A pharmacist reviews medications, bloodwork can be ordered, and the centre offers Suboxone assessment for people with opioid use disorder. It also arranges quick access to EMDR therapy for trauma.

The website lists $16,000 plus GST for the first four months, with a $500 plus GST intake deposit applied to that cost, and lower fees after month four. It is private pay. The team also includes a social worker, a nurse in client relations, a Cree Elder who leads sweat lodge ceremonies, a breathwork practitioner and a yoga instructor.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Executive Medical Solutions

faqs.question: Is Executive Medical Solutions a residential rehab?

answer_blocks.text: No. It is a private outpatient addiction program in Winnipeg, and you keep living at home and working while you take part. There are no beds or overnight stays. You come in for individual counselling and group sessions at 3408 Roblin Boulevard, and you can join groups virtually when you cannot get there.
answer_blocks.html: No. It is a private outpatient addiction program in Winnipeg, and you keep living at home and working while you take part. There are no beds or overnight stays. You come in for individual counselling and group sessions at 3408 Roblin Boulevard, and you can join groups virtually when you cannot get there.

answer_blocks.text: Every client gets weekly one-to-one counselling plus access to one to three groups a day. The counselling draws on DBT, CBT and other addiction-specific methods with a trauma-informed approach. The program also offers psychiatric assessment for co-occurring mental illness, pharmacist consultation, Suboxone assessment, rapid access to EMDR therapy, and yoga, breathwork and mindfulness sessions.

The centre says research links about 90 days of treatment while abstinent with better long-term recovery, and that the first month of a community program often is not fully abstinent. It suggests at least one individual session and four groups a week.

faqs.question: How much does Executive Medical Solutions cost?

answer_blocks.text: The centre's website lists $16,000 plus GST for the first four-month commitment, with a $500 plus GST intake deposit that goes toward the program cost. Recovery.com lists that as $4,000 a month for the first four months and about $1,000 a month after that. Months after the first four cost less, and the centre asks you to contact it to confirm current prices.

faqs.question: Is it covered by Manitoba Health?

answer_blocks.text: The program is private pay. Neither the centre's website nor its recovery.com profile lists Manitoba Health coverage or direct insurance billing. If you hope to claim part of it through workplace or extended health benefits, ask your insurer what it covers for psychiatry, social work and counselling before you pay the deposit.

faqs.question: Can I get Suboxone or medical care for co-occurring mental health conditions?

answer_blocks.text: Yes, through assessment. Psychiatrist Dr. Jeffrey Waldman is certified by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Manitoba to provide opioid agonist therapy (Suboxone), and the centre offers psychiatric assessment, usually in the first week of the program. Bloodwork can be ordered to check for medical problems linked to substance use, and you can use your own pharmacy or the one the centre partners with.

faqs.question: Does Executive Medical Solutions offer detox?

answer_blocks.text: Its website does not describe a medical detox or withdrawal unit, and there are no beds on site. If you drink heavily every day or use opioids, benzodiazepines or other drugs with risky withdrawal, talk to your doctor or Manitoba's public withdrawal services before you start. The centre's Suboxone assessment is a separate service for opioid use disorder.
